text.tspan: Branching strategies: trunk-based (what I'd pick for CI/CD) vs GitFlow
Trunk-based development (+ short-lived feature branches)
main: protected, always deployable (merge = MR + CI + review)
feature/login (1-2 days)
fix/JIRA-42
Release = tag v1.4.0 on main (build once)
same image promoted dev → uat → prod
unfinished work hidden behind feature flags
hotfix: branch from main (or the tag), MR, tag again
GitFlow
main: production releases only (tags)
release/1.4: stabilise, then merge to main + develop
develop: integration branch
feature/*: from develop, back to develop
hotfix/*: from main, merged to main + develop
How to answer: "We used trunk-based with short-lived feature branches and merge requests into a protected main.
Every MR runs the pipeline; merge needs 1 approval + green CI. Images are tagged with the commit SHA and promoted
through environments by GitOps, so we never rebuild per branch. GitFlow suits versioned products with scheduled
releases; it slows continuous delivery (long-lived branches, painful merges)."
Protect main: no direct push, required review, required pipeline, squash or merge commits, signed commits optional
